rounds.text: Unihealth Hospitals Ltd demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency, boasting a phenomenal Return on Equity of 38.04% and a Return on Capital Employed of 33.03%, both vastly outperforming their respective sector benchmarks of 10.37% and 11.95% [E9, E10]. This fundamental business strength is underpinned by explosive top- and bottom-line expansion, highlighted by compounded sales growth of 44% over three years and an extraordinary trailing twelve-month profit growth of 81% [E15, E19]. The company trades at a highly attractive EV/EBITDA of 10.05x compared to the sector benchmark of 17.13x, while its P/E ratio of 22.03x sits comfortably below the sector's 32.16x [E6, E11]. Adding to this compelling valuation disconnect, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 1179 per share against a market price of Rs 521, providing a massive 55.8% margin of safety [E41, E42]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF reveals that the current market price only prices in a modest 6.8% earnings growth, drastically underestimating the company's proven trajectory [E43]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased to 64.82% while cash conversion remains low at 0.13x alongside high debtors of 341 days [E29, E37, E59].

The valuation and quality of earnings are severely disconnected, as evidenced by a terrible cash conversion ratio of 0.13x in March 2026 where reported profits far outstrip actual operating cash flow [E29]. This shortfall translates into a negative free cash flow of -Rs 26 Cr [E31], while borrowings climbed from Rs 22 Cr to Rs 33 Cr [E35] alongside alarmingly high debtor days of 341 [E59]. Institutional confidence is actively fleeing the stock, marked by sharp drops in foreign holdings from 5.61% to 0.01% and domestic holdings from 3.31% to 0.45% since September 2023 [E38, E39], accompanied by negative money flow signals [E40]. Promoter ownership has also steadily eroded from 68.80% to 64.82% over the same period [E37], and quarterly operating margins contracted by 5 percentage points year-over-year [E26]. Furthermore, recent price growth has outpaced profit growth by 136% in a price-led move that leaves expectations dangerously ahead of delivery [E53], compounded by a high annualized volatility of 69.6% [E50] and zero dividend payout [E4, E56]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical sales and profit growth, robust ROE and ROCE figures well above sector benchmarks, and a high relative-strength rating [E8, E9, E10, E14, E17, E47].

Conceded: cash conversion is 0.13x [E29], free cash flow is -Rs 26 Cr [E31], and borrowings increased to Rs 33 Cr alongside high debtor days [E35, E59]. Conceded: institutional and promoter holdings have decreased [E37, E38, E39], quarterly margins contracted [E26], volatility is high [E50], and there is zero dividend [E4]. However, these headwinds are overwhelmingly offset by massive fundamental outperformance, including a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 1179 offering a 55.8% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 521 [E41, E42]. The company commands a stellar return on equity of 38.04% and ROCE of 33.03% compared to sector benchmarks of 10.37% and 11.95% [E9, E10], while achieving a rules-based screen score of 87 out of 100 with a BUY rating [E60]. Furthermore, compounded sales growth of 38% over five years and 44% over three years [E14, E15] dwarf the sector median sales growth of 17.4% [E71], proving that exceptional underlying momentum easily eclipses short-term cash flow friction.

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 1179 per share [E41], and compounded sales growth figures of 38% over five years and 44% over three years outperform the sector median of 17.4% [E14, E15, E71]. However, that high intrinsic value relies on assumptions that conflict with the severe reality of a cash conversion ratio of just 0.13x and a negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr in Mar 2026 [E29, E31]. Furthermore, pointing to a rules-based screen score of 87 [E60] ignores the internal contradictions within those very signals, which explicitly warn of decelerating earnings growth and negative institutional money flow [E40, E65]. The impressive-looking returns on equity and capital [E9, E10] are undermined by high debtors stretching to 341 days [E59] and a low tax rate flag [E58], raising questions about the actual quality of reported profits. Finally, price growth has raced 136% ahead of profit growth recently, and expectations are running far ahead of delivery while smart money exits the stock [E38, E39, E53].
